title: Our City, Our Schools
description: Washington, DC's history, neighborhoods, and schools, and where KIPP DC fits in.
objectives: Describe the demographic, economic, and cultural context of Washington, DC.
Summarize the history of DC's public education system and the consequences of systemic under-investment.
Explain DC's dual education landscape and what research says about student outcomes.
Identify KIPP DC's origins, mission, and role in the broader DC education ecosystem.
Articulate why historical knowledge of DC is relevant to your daily work as a resident teacher.

blocks.text: Washington, DC is the seat of federal power. It is also a predominantly Black city with a deep history of resistance.

items: DC has no voting representation in Congress, despite having a larger population than two states.
DC has one of the highest income inequality rates of any major American city.
Nearly 1 in 5 DC children lives in poverty.

blocks.text: This is the city your students are growing up in. Understanding it is part of your job.
Wards east of the Anacostia River have historically been under-resourced, over-policed, and underserved by public institutions, including schools.
This doesn't mean your students are defined by their zip codes.

blocks.text: DC ran a segregated school system. Black schools were sites of excellence, staffed by highly educated Black teachers who knew their students and communities.
Brown v. Board (1954) and what was lost
Desegregation was a landmark victory, and it came at a cost, including the mass dismissal of Black teachers.

blocks.label: Listen: Revisionist History, "Miss Buchanan's Period of Adjustment" (Malcolm Gladwell)

blocks.text: By the 1990s, DCPS was described as "educationally and managerially bankrupt."
1996 legislation created the DC Public Charter School Board. Charters served over 27% of students by 2007 and close to half today.
In 2007, Mayor Adrian Fenty and Chancellor Michelle Rhee launched an era of reform, including the IMPACT teacher evaluation system.

blocks.label: Read: A Tale of Two Systems

blocks.title: Key Idea
blocks.text: Reform in DC was never just about data. It was always about race, power, and who gets to decide what's best for children.
KIPP was founded in 1994 by Mike Feinberg and Dave Levin. KIPP DC opened its first school in 2001.

blocks.text: Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose — college, career, and beyond — so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

questions.prompt: Which of the following best describes the economic landscape of Washington, DC?

options.text: DC's poverty rate is lower than most major American cities
DC has high income inequality, with extreme wealth and concentrated poverty coexisting
DC is a uniformly wealthy city with few low-income residents

questions.explanation: DC has one of the highest income inequality rates of any major American city.

questions.prompt: What does research tell us about the impact of having a Black teacher on Black students?

options.text: There is no measurable difference in outcomes based on teacher race
Black students with at least one Black teacher are significantly more likely to graduate from high school and aspire to college
The impact only applies to students in elementary school

questions.explanation: Having even one Black teacher raises Black students' graduation rates and college aspirations.

questions.prompt: According to A Tale of Two Systems, what was the primary reason DCPS was labeled "educationally and managerially bankrupt" in the 1990s?

options.text: Significant underfunding relative to other major American cities
Decades of political corruption, patronage hiring, and systemic disinvestment in students
A lack of student motivation and family engagement in DC communities

questions.explanation: The reading points to political corruption, patronage hiring, and systemic disinvestment, not students or families.

questions.prompt: What does KIPP DC's mission mean when it says "the paths they choose"?

options.text: KIPP DC guides all students toward four-year college as the primary pathway
KIPP DC gives students skills and confidence to pursue their own paths: college, career, and beyond
KIPP DC allows students to opt out of academic expectations based on personal preference

questions.explanation: The mission is about students choosing their own paths, with the skills and confidence to pursue them.
